module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Ringel's Conjecture

*Reference:* G. Ringel, *Problem 25*, in *Theory of Graphs and its Applications*
(Proc. Sympos. Smolenice, 1963), Academia, Prague, 1964.

Ringel's conjecture (1963): the complete graph $K_{2n+1}$ decomposes into copies of any tree
with $n$ edges. It remains open; the case of all sufficiently large $n$ is proved by
Montgomery–Pokrovskiy–Sudakov, see `Arxiv/2001.02665/RingelConjecture.lean`.
-/

@[expose] public section
namespace RingelConjecture

open SimpleGraph

/--
For any tree $T$ with $n$ edges, the complete graph $K_{2n+1}$ decomposes into
$2n+1$ edge-disjoint copies of $T$.

A "copy" of $T$ is the image $T.\text{map}(f_i)$ of $T$ under a vertex embedding
$f_i : V \hookrightarrow \text{Fin}(2n+1)$; the copies are pairwise edge-disjoint
and together cover every edge of $K_{2n+1}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem ringel_conjecture {V : Type} [Finite V]
    (T : SimpleGraph V) (hT : T.IsTree)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : T.edgeSet.ncard = n) :
    ∃ f : Fin (2 * n + 1) → (V ↪ Fin (2 * n + 1)),
      Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (T.map (f i)).edgeSet (T.map (f j)).edgeSet) ∧
      ⨆ i, T.map (f i) = (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin (2 * n + 1))) := by
  sorry

end RingelConjecture

reformulations.difference: The source says: "the complete graph K_{2n+1} can be decomposed into copies of any tree with n edges". A decomposition partitions the edges of K_{2n+1} into subgraphs isomorphic to T; the source does not fix how many. The Lean fixes exactly 2n+1 copies, indexed by `Fin (2 * n + 1)`. Each copy is the image graph `T.map (f i)` of a vertex embedding `f i : V ↪ Fin (2 * n + 1)`, not a subgraph with an isomorphism to T. "Decomposition" is written as pairwise disjoint `edgeSet`s plus `⨆ i, T.map (f i) = ⊤`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (1) Copies. A subgraph of K_m isomorphic to T is exactly `Copy.toSubgraph` of an injective map V → Fin m (Mathlib `SimpleGraph.Copy.range_toSubgraph`). Its edge set equals `(T.map g).edgeSet`, by `Subgraph.edgeSet_map` and `SimpleGraph.edgeSet_map`. Also `edgeSet_iSup` turns `⨆ = ⊤` into "the union of the edge sets is all of E(K_m)". (2) Number of copies. Each copy has n edges and K_{2n+1} has (2n+1)n edges. So for n ≥ 1 any decomposition, with any finite index type, has exactly 2n+1 parts, and it can be reindexed by `Fin (2n+1)`. (3) Boundary case n = 0. T is a single vertex and K_1 has no edges, so both sides hold trivially. I proved all of this in Lean with no `sorry` (axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). The main theorem, `ringel_statement_iff_literal` in /workspace/review/combined.lean, has the file's exact type on the left. On the right is a literal decomposition statement `LiteralDecomp T (2n+1)`: there are a finite type ι and subgraphs `H : ι → (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin (2n+1))).Subgraph` with `Nonempty (T ≃g (H i).coe)`, pairwise disjoint edge sets, and `⋃ i, (H i).edgeSet = ⊤.edgeSet`. The MPS abstract itself also phrases the conjecture as "any tree with n edges packs 2n+1 times into K_{2n+1}".

review.notes:
I checked the one declaration, `RingelConjecture.ringel_conjecture`, and found no misformalization. Lean checks (scratch files in /workspace/review/):
(a) The conclusion elaborates as `Eq (iSup fun i => map (f i) T) ⊤`, an equality of graphs. It does not parse as a supremum of propositions.
(b) The n = 0 case is provable in a few lines. It is trivially true: T is one vertex and K_1 has no edges.
(c) The conclusion is satisfiable, and I proved it with `decide` for K_2 in K_3, the 3-vertex path in K_5, and K_{1,3} in K_7, using cyclic shifts of graceful labelings. A constant family of embeddings fails disjointness, so the statement is neither vacuous nor trivial for n ≥ 1.
(d) The file's exact statement is equivalent to a literal \"edge partition into subgraphs isomorphic to T\" version of Ringel's conjecture (`ringel_statement_iff_literal`, no `sorry`).
Hypotheses: `V : Type` rather than `Type*` loses nothing, since every finite tree is isomorphic to one on `Fin k`. `[Finite V]` is present, so `edgeSet.ncard` is the true edge count. `IsTree` includes `Nonempty V` through `Connected`.
Status: the `research open` tag is right for the all-n statement. MPS (GAFA 2021) and Keevash–Staden (JEMS 2025) prove it only for sufficiently large n, and Gallian's 2025 survey still says 'for large n'. Wikipedia's 'List of unsolved problems in mathematics' files Ringel's conjecture under 'Problems solved since 2015', and the Keevash–Staden abstract says it 'establishes a conjecture of Ringel'. Both are loose wording; neither changes the status of the all-n statement.
Docstrings are accurate. The 'Problem 25, Smolenice 1963, Prague 1964' citation matches Gallian's.
Limits of my checks: I could not read Ringel's 1964 problem text itself, so I relied on MPS and Gallian quoting it. The arXiv search API returned HTTP 429 every time, so my check for a post-2021 all-n proof rests on the Crossref searches and Gallian's 2025 survey. Neither shows one.
